title: Canonical RHom scalar-extension map on perfect representatives
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Regard modules over these rings as sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on their one-object bottom-topology sites. Let $H_A(P,Q)=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,Q)$ be the shared Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex], with its actual product projections, and let $R\operatorname{Hom}_A$ be [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Package the extension functor $T_\varphi$, with its objects and maps exactly those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and its left derived functor $L_\varphi$ and K-flat counit $\epsilon$ as in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The canonical chain map $\chi_{P,Q}:T_\varphi H_A(P,Q)\to H_B(T_\varphi P,T_\varphi Q)$ is specified in degree $n$, at every product coordinate $p$, by $b\otimes f\mapsto(c\otimes x\mapsto bc\otimes f_p(x))$, using the sheafification units of the shared scalar extension. Let $E,K\in D(A)$ with $E$ represented by a bounded complex of finite projective modules. Choose such a representative $P$ of $E$ and a K-flat representative $Q$ of $K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] and [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Write $r_A:R\operatorname{Hom}_A(E,K)\cong Q_A H_A(P,Q)$ for the shared localization factorization through the functorial K-injective replacement, followed by the inverse of $Q_A\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,Q\to I(Q))$ and transport along the representative isomorphisms; define $r_B$ analogously on $T_\varphi P,T_\varphi Q$, transporting the representative isomorphisms by the actual counit. The canonical perfect-source base-change map is the composite $L_\varphi R\operatorname{Hom}_A(E,K)\xrightarrow{L_\varphi(r_A)}L_\varphi Q_AH_A(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\epsilon}Q_BT_\varphi H_A(P,Q)\xrightarrow{Q_B\chi}Q_BH_B(T_\varphi P,T_\varphi Q)\xrightarrow{r_B^{-1}}R\operatorname{Hom}_B(L_\varphi E,L_\varphi K)$. This is the $B$-linear extension of the map induced by scalar extension, and introduces no boundedness assumption on $K$ or flatness assumption on $\varphi$.

proof.text: For ringHomReplacement_quasiIso, install the proved quasi-isomorphism of the functorial K-injective resolution map. Apply bounded exact-term Hom preservation to P with its original bounds, supplying exactness for every term by ringProjectiveInternalHomExact. Finite generation is not used. The resolution and bounded-Hom theorem are existing library declarations.

For perfectRHomBaseChangeModel_exists, unpack the perfect-source hypothesis into P and its bounds, finiteness, projectivity and source isomorphism. Apply ringBoundedProjectiveExtension to obtain K-flatness of P and projectivity of its extension. Choose the ordinary complex representative Q0 of K provided by essential surjectivity of Q and a K-flat resolution s:Q→Q0. The derived image of s is invertible, so compose its asIso with the original representative isomorphism to obtain targetIso.

The counit fields of d are isomorphisms on P and Q by their K-flatness. Unfold ringDerivedExtensionCounit: the other three factors are functor images of isomorphisms and quotient-factorization isomorphisms, so the composite is invertible. An additive functor preserves zero objects, giving the extended bounds directly from the same endpoints. Fill all fields of PerfectRHomBaseChangeModel with these values.

The existing localization/model-isomorphism and canonical map definitions remain unchanged. ringRHomBaseChangeData_exists remains an unfinished named theorem with the construction and differential calculation described in its original docstring.
